title: Stage 1: Types and Validation
summary: Model tasks with union and literal types, and create them safely from untrusted input.

steps.title: The project
body: Over five stages you will build the **core** of a task board (think Trello): everything except the screen. In a React or Next.js app this is the code in `lib/board.ts` that components import. Keeping it pure and typed means the UI is thin and the logic is tested.
Stage 1 is the **domain model**: what a task is, and how one is created from form input that may be wrong.
- `createTask` returns a `Result<Task>` rather than throwing: bad input is an expected outcome.
- The id and the time are **passed in**. That keeps `createTask` pure and deterministic (the UI would pass `crypto.randomUUID()` and `Date.now()`).

steps.prompt: Why does `createTask(input, id, now)` take `id` and `now` as parameters instead of calling `crypto.randomUUID()` and `Date.now()` itself?
options: So it is pure: the same inputs always give the same task, which makes it testable and safe to use in a reducer

steps.title: createTask
prompt: Write the domain types and `createTask(input: NewTask, id: string, now: number): Result<Task>`.
readonly id: string; title: string; status: Status; priority: Priority;
type NewTask = { title: string; priority?: Priority; tags?: string[] };
type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; errors: string[] };
- `title` is trimmed and must be 1 to 100 characters, else error `"title"` (also when it is not a string at all: input may come from JSON)
- `priority` defaults to `"medium"`; any other value than the three priorities gives error `"priority"`
- errors are listed in that order
- `tags` are trimmed, lower-cased, empty ones dropped, duplicates removed (first occurrence kept); default `[]`
solution: type NewTask = { title: string; priority?: Priority; tags?: string[] };
type Result<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; errors: string[] };
function createTask(input: NewTask, id: string, now: number): Result<Task> {
return { ok: true, value: { id, title, status: "todo", priority, tags, createdAt: now } };
template: const dojoOk = createTask({ title: "  Write tests ", tags: ["Dev", " dev", "", "UI"] }, "t1", 1000);
Dojo.eq("valid task", { ok: true, value: { id: "t1", title: "Write tests", status: "todo", priority: "medium", tags: ["dev", "ui"], createdAt: 1000 } }, dojoOk);
Dojo.eq("priority kept", "high", (createTask({ title: "Ship", priority: "high" }, "t2", 5) as any).value?.priority);
Dojo.eq("empty title", { ok: false, errors: ["title"] }, createTask({ title: "   " }, "x", 0));
Dojo.eq("101-character title", { ok: false, errors: ["title"] }, createTask({ title: "a".repeat(101) }, "x", 0));
Dojo.eq("100-character title is fine", true, createTask({ title: "a".repeat(100) }, "x", 0).ok);
Dojo.eq("bad priority and title from bad JSON", { ok: false, errors: ["title", "priority"] }, createTask({ title: 42, priority: "urgent" } as any, "x", 0));
Dojo.eq("no tags gives []", [], (createTask({ title: "a" }, "x", 0) as any).value?.tags);
hints: Collect errors in an array; return `{ ok: false, errors }` if any.
